title: Glass Bridge Stepper
lead: A fair crash ladder. Ten rungs, cash out any time. Survival to rung k is RTP ÷ payoutₖ, so every stopping rule returns the same 97%: the player chooses variance, never expectation.
figures: Returns, survival and the single-RN crash table for the three difficulties.
Monte Carlo under four stopping rules: every one returns the RTP.
Where the crash falls: the eleven slots of the single draw.

title: Red Light Green Light
lead: A single-shot payout function. The field is the 0–10000 draw; zone widths are the probabilities; inside a zone the payout ramps from a − r to a + r. Payouts and RTP in, a monotone payout(u) out, exact by summation.
figures: Same payouts, same RTP, same r under three probability assignments. Only the zone widths move.
Inside every band the paid multiple is exactly uniform on [a − r, a + r].

title: Rated Racers
lead: A Plackett–Luce race. Racers carry an Elo; strength is 10^(Elo/400); the next finisher is drawn in proportion to strength. Every ordered podium has a closed-form probability and one draw picks it. Odds are set so every racer returns exactly the RTP, winner-only or 1st/2nd/3rd.
figures: Place probabilities per racer and the outcome zones on the draw, sorted by probability.
